acceptance.given: The replay implementation serializes or interprets a terminal result using the declared terminal categories and any supported serialized aliases.

oracle.expected: A real replay invocation accepts only pass, comparison-failed, invalid-input, identity-invalid, evidence-invalid, stale, execution-failed, timed-out, and permitted expected-difference cases; aliases round-trip to the same declared category without changing success or failure semantics.
forbidden: An undeclared terminal category is emitted or accepted as a successful result.
A serialized alias maps any failure category to pass or otherwise merges failure into success.
A declared terminal category is silently reinterpreted as a different category.
oracle.observable: The replay receipt and its parsed terminal result expose the declared canonical category, and alias normalization yields the same category and success/failure classification.

acceptance.then: The validator executes the terminal-category and alias assertions against the production replay entry point and records a deterministic pass only when all category and alias semantics remain intact.
acceptance.when: When serializing or interpreting a terminal replay result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py mutates a terminal result to an undeclared category and verifies the replay contract rejects it.
scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py maps a declared failure alias to pass and verifies the replay contract rejects the semantic merge.
scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py maps an alias to a different declared terminal category and verifies silent reinterpretation is rejected.

affected_subjects: Terminal result serialization and interpretation in the shared replay pipeline
slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce the declared terminal-category set and canonical alias semantics at replay-result serialization and interpretation, preserving each category's success or failure meaning.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing canonical terminal categories and their failure/success classifications remain unchanged; rollback removes only the new rejection/alias enforcement while preserving receipt compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: A terminal replay result is serialized or parsed; category validation and alias normalization produce a canonical declared category or a deterministic rejection.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The terminal result is successful only if its canonical category belongs to the declared set and every alias resolves to that same category and success/failure classification; otherwise the invocation fails closed.

acceptance.given: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages participate in one Toolchain evaluation or rollback workflow.

oracle.expected: The isolation boundary check shows independently controlled mutable state and evidence for every listed component, with no cross-component contamination path.
forbidden: Any listed component shares mutable state with another listed component.
Cross-component mutable-state sharing permits one component to alter another component's execution or result.
oracle.observable: The isolation-boundary inspection and the cross-component substitution witness evaluated during matrix execution.

acceptance.then: Each component operates only on independently controlled mutable state and evidence.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain runs or rolls back the participating components and evaluates the isolation boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Inject a cross-component mutable evidence substitution and require the isolation check to reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Partition mutable state and evidence for Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages, rejecting cross-component evidence substitution.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing replay results remain compatible; contamination is rejected rather than represented as success.

slice_hint.state_transition: Shared evaluation workflow with isolation required -> independently owned mutable state and evidence for all participating components.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The boundary check rejects a cross-component state or evidence substitution and finds no mutable-state sharing among the listed components.

acceptance.given: A frozen non-empty Consumer Manifest and the reconciled repository real-call surface, including VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing consumers, are available.

oracle.expected: Every applicable Consumer completes enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable through its real call surface; rollback observes the Prior Route identity and Prior Behavior Baseline verdict and diagnostic category.
forbidden: A manifest entry lacks a reconciled real caller.
Configuration-only switching is accepted as rollback.
oracle.observable: Per-Consumer transition call receipts and the bidirectional Consumer Manifest/call-surface reconciliation.

acceptance.then: All applicable transitions for every non-empty Consumer Manifest entry are complete.
acceptance.when: The Consumer transition selector executes against the frozen manifest.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the Consumer transition selector with one applicable real-call-surface transition omitted or unreachable.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reconcile the complete non-empty Consumer Manifest bidirectionally with the repository real-call surface, then require each applicable Consumer to execute enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable through its real interface.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing Consumer routes and require rollback to reproduce the bound Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category.

slice_hint.state_transition: Frozen manifest with applicable transitions pending -> every applicable Consumer has real-call receipts for enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector proves 100% transition completion for the reconciled non-empty manifest and rejects omissions, unreachable consumers, and configuration-only rollback.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result succeeds for an input whose Validator Capability is independently evaluable.

oracle.expected: The replay result includes a Validator Capability verification outcome produced for that result, independently of other replay verifications.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result whose Validator Capability verification is inferred from another verification.
oracle.observable: The successful replay result's per-result Validator Capability verification outcome.

acceptance.then: The successful Replay Result carries its own Validator Capability verification outcome.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the S24 replay behavior test with a successful replay whose Validator Capability outcome is omitted or borrowed; the runtime assertion must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each successful replay result to independently verify and expose its Validator Capability outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore prior replay-result verification handling without changing the capability descriptor schema.

slice_hint.state_transition: successful replay without independent capability verification -> successful replay with a per-result independent capability outcome
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S24 selector rejects a successful replay that lacks its own Validator Capability verification.
